# Counterparty Channel Discipline

Curated by Skill Harbor: a written workflow contract for agents that sit in shared channels with external counterparties such as customers, suppliers, or partners. It keeps three things strictly separate: audience classification, participation consent, and permission to send. Default posture is require_mention in external groups, so the agent speaks only when explicitly addressed and stays silent otherwise; deliberate silence is a valid outcome. Reasoning, stack traces, secrets, host paths, and internal filing notices are never counterparty content. Prices, contractual language, legal matters, public posts, and unverified claims stay draft-only for operator approval. Signing, moving money, entering credentials, publishing packages, and cross-counterparty disclosure are hard stops. Output is re-checked after formatting, before every send, edit, or stream fragment. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: this is a written contract for the runtime that owns messaging, not an executable transport guard; enforcement depends on the owning runtime actually implementing the gates. A passing prompt test alone does not prove enforcement. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
